script.base: Detroit is -10 with a 27.2 implied total in a dome, so the book has DET leading by halftime and closing a moderate game (total 44.5) on the ground. Cleveland (17.2) falls behind and throws; Judkins' recent 14-carry rate (28 carries, 155 yards across the two listed games) gets cut after the first half. Detroit's committee (Gibbs 43 carries, Montgomery 34) runs late, but Cleveland's rush defense (2.49 YPC, 2 runs of 10+) caps efficiency so late carries do not automatically clear rushing lines.
script.flip1: Cleveland hangs around into the fourth because Flacco avoids the Detroit blitz that has produced -0.58 EPA/db. Judkins keeps a full carry script and his 5.5 YPC, so the rush under dies; Detroit never gets a clock-kill series, so Montgomery does not get a carry spike either.
script.flip2: Detroit is up three scores by half. Cleveland abandons the run entirely (Judkins under strengthens) and dumps to TEs and backs. Detroit sits Gibbs, Montgomery and St. Brown late, so Montgomery can finish under 57.5 on early work only, or he is already over if a first-half explosive landed before the sit.

matchup.shell: No man/zone, MOFO/MOFC or coverage charting in the pack. Location splits only: DET defense YPA left 8.74 (31 att), middle 12.14 (21), right 5.94 (31). CLE defense YPA left 7.27 (30), middle 10.0 (7, small sample), right 5.82 (40).
matchup.pressure: DET blitzes 44%; Cleveland EPA/db is -0.58 vs blitz and -0.13 vs none, so pressure should kill Jeudy's vertical yards (21 targets, 292 air) and push checkdowns to Njoku, Fannin and the backs. CLE blitzes only 22%; Detroit EPA/db is +0.87 vs blitz and +0.24 vs none, so Goff is fine even though Cleveland rarely brings extra rushers.
matchup.bleeds: DET bleeds the middle (12.14 YPA) and has allowed 11 passes of 20+ and 10 runs of 10+ at 4.26 YPC. CLE does not bleed the run (2.49 YPC, 2 runs of 10+) and has allowed only 6 passes of 20+; the right side is the strength (5.82 YPA on 40 throws).
matchup.overlap: Cleveland's best overlap is the TE/slot middle (Njoku 18/117, Fannin 18/136) into DET's 12.14 middle YPA, plus Cunningham out and a 44% blitz. The four-way target split (Jeudy 21, Tillman 18, Njoku 18, Fannin 18) and lines pinned to the median kept that off the card. Detroit's pass overlap is St. Brown (25/237) into a low-blitz CLE defense, but 77.5 equals his median (45, 115, 77). The rush overlap that makes the card is Montgomery's explosive-dependent yards into a CLE front that has allowed two 10+ runs.

Implied 27.2 is enough for a clock-kill, but 44.5 is not a shootout, so volume overs are not automatic. Blowout flag is live at -10: Detroit skill-position snaps can get cut if it is 28+ early, which threatens overs more than unders. Usage from shares, not raw averages: Judkins has the CLE carry share in the window (28); Gibbs 43 and Montgomery 34 split DET rushes; St. Brown's 25 targets are the only clear DET pass share.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost because the game stayed within a score into the fourth, not a Detroit control script. Judkins got his 14 carries plus a 20-yard run the Detroit front has been allowing (10 explosives, 4.26 YPC) and finished in the mid-80s. Montgomery did not need 20 carries: Hall was out, the interior gave him one crease Cleveland's three-game sample had not shown, and 57.5 was gone by halftime. Conklin and Decker both played, so the tackle question marks never showed up. The lines were the medians; there was no price to be right about.
slip_story: One story: moderate Detroit control in a dome (favorite 27.2, dog 17.2, total 44.5), not a shootout and not a 35-point sit-fest. Cleveland's run game dies with the script (Judkins rush under); Detroit's run game is capped by Cleveland's front (Montgomery rush under). Do not pair these with CLE receiver overs or a game over — those need the close-game or shootout flip. Do not add a Gibbs rush over; it needs the opposite efficiency read. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player. They fit a 7-14 point Detroit lead and break if it is a shootout (both unders lose) or a 30-point blowout (Judkins under strengthens, Montgomery becomes snap-risk noise).
